title: the curve 11a1
blurb: given by its equation; conductor 11, the smallest over Q
reference: [IUTchI] Def 3.1 (a)–(f); F chosen as in [IUTchIV] Thm 1.10
tuple: (F̄/F, X_F, l, C̲_K, V, V^bad_mod, ε̲)

Fmod.why: F_mod is the field of moduli Q(j) of X_F, and j ∈ Q

Ftpd.why: ψ₂ = 4x³ − 4x² − 40x − 79 has no rational root, and Δ = -161051 is not a square, so Gal(Q(E[2])/Q) ≅ S3

F.FBar: an algebraic closure Q̄ of Q (hence of F)
F.why: Gal(F/F_tpd) embeds in {±1} × GL2(F_3) × GL2(F_5), of order 2·48·480 = 46080; [F_tpd:Q] = 6
F.stableReduction: Raynaud: E[3] ⊆ E(F) ⇒ semistable at every v ∤ 3, E[5] ⊆ E(F) ⇒ semistable at every v ∤ 5

X_F.E_F: y² + y = x³ − x² − 10x − 20, base-changed to F

reasons: F ⊇ Q(E[5]) acts trivially on E[5], so the image cannot contain SL2(F_5)
l = 11 is a residue characteristic of V^bad_mod

SL2.criterion: Serre 1972 §2.8 Prop 19: elements s, s′, s″ in the image force it to contain SL2(F_l)
SL2.overF: [F:Q] | 276480 is prime to l, so Im(G_F) is normal of index prime to l in Im(G_Q) ⊇ SL2(F_l), hence also ⊇ SL2(F_l)

K.why: F is unramified at 7 (ramified only over 2, 3, 5 and the primes of Δ), so F ∩ Q(μ_7) = Q and det = cyclotomic character is onto F_7^×

C_K.XUnderK: X̲_K of type (1, l-tors): the Z/7-cover of X_K cut out by a surjection E[7] ↠ Q ≅ Z/7Z
C_K.why: the kernel of E[7] ↠ Q is one of the 8 lines of E[7] ≅ F_7²; all are K-rational because K = F(E[7])
C_K.kCore: C_F: j ∉ Z (some ord_p(j) < 0) while CM j-invariants are algebraic integers, so E has no CM and the K-core of C̲_K is C_F ([CanLift] Rem 2.1.1)

V.rule: one place v of K above each place of F_mod = Q (a section of V(K) ↠ V_mod); for v ∈ V^bad choose v so that the kernel of E[l] ↠ Q is the Tate subgroup μ_l (type (1, Z/lZ)±) — possible because Gal(K/F) ⊇ SL2(F_l) moves any line to any other
V.otherPrimes: every other prime p: E has good reduction at p, v ∈ V^good (any v | p in K)

epsilon.why: Def 3.1 (f): a cusp from a NON-zero element of Q ≅ Z/lZ; at v ∈ V^bad it must be the cusp of the canonical generator ±1 of Z (q^{1/l})

derived.logQFormula: Σ_{v ∈ V^bad_mod} ord_v(q_v)·log p_v  (= deg of the q-divisor; [F_mod:Q] = 1)

conditions.need: F a number field with √−1 ∈ F; F̄ an algebraic closure
conditions.how: F = Q(√−1, E[2·3·5]) contains √−1 by construction

conditions.need: X_F once-punctured elliptic curve with stable reduction at every finite v; F/F_mod Galois of degree prime to l; E[2·3] ⊆ E(F); V^bad_mod ≠ ∅, odd, multiplicative
l ≥ 5 prime, Im(G_F → GL2(F_l)) ⊇ SL2(F_l), l prime to V^bad_mod and to every ord(q_v)
C̲_K of type (1, l-tors)± with K-core C_F
conditions.how: choose one of the 8 lines of E[7]; j ∉ Z so E has no CM

conditions.need: V ⊆ V(K) a section of V(K) ↠ V_mod; at v ∈ V^bad, C̲_v of type (1, Z/lZ)±
conditions.how: one v | p per p; at V^bad the v of the Tate μ_l

conditions.need: ε̲ a cusp of C̲_K from a nonzero element of Q

thm110Hypothesis.statement: E_F has good reduction at every v ∈ V(F)^good ∩ V(F)^non not dividing 2l ([IUTchIV] Thm 1.10)
thm110Hypothesis.why: V^bad_mod contains every odd prime where E_F is bad over F
